channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Invests Billions in Gas Plant Construction: Who Benefits?
item.description: Kazakhstan is undertaking multi-billion dollar investments in the construction of gas plants. The article questions the intended beneficiaries of these significant projects, implying a need for transparency and public understanding of the economic rationale behind these developments.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Proposes Stricter Control Over Electric Scooters in Bishkek
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has proposed strengthening control over electric scooters, scooters, and mopeds in Bishkek. The suggestion comes amid a rise in traffic accidents involving these vehicles, leading to injuries and fatalities. The MP called for registration, stricter rules, and potential limitations.

item.title: Trial Begins for Alleged Sexual Assault of 5-Year-Old Girl in Uzbekistan
item.description: A trial has commenced in Uzbekistan regarding the alleged sexual assault of a 5-year-old girl at a kindergarten in Uchqo‘rg‘on district, Namangan region. The case involves a 52-year-old suspect and others. The proceedings will be held in a closed session due to the victim's age.

item.title: Russia, China, US Discuss Limiting AI in Nuclear Weapons Control
item.description: Representatives from Russia, China, and the United States are discussing the possibility of a trilateral summit at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. A key topic will be the use of artificial intelligence in controlling nuclear weapons. The three nations are seeking consensus on AI's role in nuclear command and control, shifting focus from the Ukraine conflict and Korean Peninsula denuclearization.

item.title: Majority of Kazakh Families Live on Monthly Incomes Between 150,000 and 300,000 Tenge
item.description: A National Bank survey revealed that 30.9% of Kazakh families earn between 150,000 and 300,000 tenge monthly, making it the most common income bracket. Another 23.6% reported incomes between 300,000-500,000 tenge, while 13.4% earn over 500,000 tenge. A significant portion, 12.6%, earns 100,000-150,000 tenge.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves National Programs to Enhance Quality of Life and Development
item.description: Uzbekistan has adopted national programs aimed at improving living standards, advancing education and healthcare, strengthening the judicial system, and supporting local communities. Key goals include making knowledge a primary development resource, increasing life expectancy, and fostering an economy based on modern technology and high productivity.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Sweden to Launch 18-Month Pilot Migration Program
item.description: Uzbekistan and Sweden are preparing to launch a pilot program focused on migration and mobility, set to last approximately 18 months. Discussions included developing organized labor migration, legal employment mechanisms, and training skilled specialists for the Swedish labor market. The initiative may involve specialized educational programs and Swedish language training.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Reprimands Emergency Situations Minister Over Duty Failures
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has issued a stern reprimand to Kanatbek Chynybaev, the Minister of Emergency Situations, for failing to properly execute his official duties. The administration of the head of state confirmed the disciplinary action, though specific violations were not detailed.

item.title: Three Officials Fired, Case Opened After 14-Year-Old's Death in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Following the death of 14-year-old Amir Kunakunov, three senior officials in Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations have been dismissed, and a criminal case for negligence has been initiated. The Minister received a stern reprimand. An investigation revealed serious shortcomings in the ministry's response and coordination.

item.title: Kazakhstan Film About Holodomor, 'Kul'pash', Premiere Canceled Days Before Release
item.description: The premiere of the Kazakh historical drama 'Kul'pash', set to depict the Holodomor tragedy, was unexpectedly canceled just hours before its scheduled release. The film's distributor cited 'necessary procedures' as the reason, sparking speculation about potential censorship or approval issues regarding the sensitive historical subject matter.

item.title: Kazakhstan Audit Reveals 47 Billion Tenge Wasted on Ineffective Science Projects
item.description: An audit in Kazakhstan uncovered financial irregularities totaling 51 billion tenge in the science sector, with 47 billion tenge identified as inefficiently planned and spent. The Supreme Audit Chamber's chairman, Alikhan Smailov, reported these findings, highlighting issues in project funding mechanisms and the disbursement of funds.

item.title: Manas Airport to Construct 40,000 Square Meter Modern Cargo Terminal
item.description: Manas International Airport plans to build a modern cargo terminal spanning 40,000 square meters. The project aims to create an international logistics hub for transporting goods from China through Kyrgyzstan to Europe and the Middle East. The terminal will be funded by the airport's own resources and will include bonded warehouses compliant with international standards.

item.title: Russia's Saratov Region Expands List of Professions Banned for Migrants
item.description: Saratov Oblast in Russia will impose new restrictions on foreign workers starting January 1, 2027, banning migrants on patents from working in energy, water supply, and freight transport. This expands previous bans in sectors like catering, taxis, and education. Similar restrictions will also be implemented in the Khanty-Mansiysk Autonomous Okrug.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes International Program for Mountainous Countries' Organic Agriculture at COP31
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed developing an international program titled "Organic Territories of Mountain Countries" for 2027-2032 at the COP31 climate conference. The initiative aims to unite efforts for organic agriculture development and climate resilience in mountainous nations, with plans for pilot organic zones and attracting international climate funds.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Participates in CSTO Meeting in Moscow
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister, Sirojiddin Mukhriddin, attended a joint meeting of the CSTO Council of Foreign Ministers, Council of Defense Ministers, and Committee of Secretaries of Security Councils in Moscow on November 10, 2026. Discussions focused on cooperation within the CSTO, the upcoming Council session agenda, and regional and international security. Draft documents to strengthen security and prevent cross-border threats were approved.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Urges Special Electricity Regime for High-Altitude Areas This Winter
item.description: A Member of Parliament has urged the Ministry of Energy to establish a special electricity supply regime for Kyrgyzstan's high-altitude regions for the upcoming winter. Citing early frosts in Naryn region, the MP highlighted the need for proactive measures, recalling last winter's power limitations and subsequent adjustments. He proposed avoiding restrictions or creating a separate regime for these areas.

item.title: State Audit Reveals 51 Billion Tenge in Violations within Kazakhstan's Science Sector
item.description: A state audit in Kazakhstan has uncovered financial violations totaling 51 billion tenge within the science sector. The Supreme Audit Chamber reported that materials from three cases will be transferred to law enforcement agencies for further investigation.

item.title: Timur Turlov Enters Agribusiness by Acquiring 51% Stake in Grain Holding
item.description: Entrepreneur Timur Turlov's company, Turlov Private Holding, intends to acquire at least 51% of Ak Zhaiyk Capital, the parent company of "Kazakhstan Grain Consortium" holding. The estimated deal value is $300 million.

item.title: Russian Interior Ministry Reports 40% Decrease in Crimes by Foreign Citizens
item.description: The number of crimes committed by foreign citizens in Russia decreased by 40% in January-September 2026 compared to the same period last year, totaling around 20,000. Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev attributed this decline to stricter migration controls. The number of foreigners banned from entering Russia also nearly doubled.

item.title: Manas Airport Installs New AI-Powered Border Control Posts
item.description: Manas International Airport in Bishkek has installed new generation border control posts equipped with modern technologies, including artificial intelligence, facial recognition, and document verification. These posts can translate up to 50 languages and enhance border control security and working conditions for officers.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP Proposes University Management System Reform
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has proposed reforming the management system of higher education institutions to improve the quality of education. The MP noted that many universities operate on a traditional system and that increased contract fees do not always correlate with improved educational quality. He suggested universities should be managed by modern, creative leaders who engage in open dialogue with students.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Proposes Parliamentary Commission into Ala-Archa Tragedy
item.description: Following the tragic death of 14-year-old Amir Kunakov in Ala-Archa, Kyrgyz MP Uulukbek Karybek uulu has called for an investigation into the Ministry of Emergency Situations' rescue efforts. He cited delays in helicopter deployment and communication issues, urging a review of protocols.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Present New Climate Initiatives and Practical Solutions at COP31
item.description: Uzbekistan will actively participate in COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, from November 9-20, 2026. The country will showcase national initiatives, projects, and experience in combating climate change, environmental protection, and transitioning to a green economy. A national pavilion will feature events with various stakeholders.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Criminal case reclassified in child sexual assault case in Kokand
item.description: The Kokand prosecutor's office has reclassified the charges against a suspect in the sexual assault of a 13-year-old girl. The suspect now faces charges of rape of a minor under 14, which carries a sentence of 15 to 25 years or life imprisonment. Previously, the charges were related to sexual relations with a minor under 16. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Nearly 51 Billion Tenge in Financial Irregularities Found in Science Sector
item.description: A state audit in Kazakhstan's science sector has uncovered financial irregularities totaling 50.9 billion tenge. An additional 47 billion tenge was found to be spent ineffectively or poorly planned. The audit covered nine government bodies and organizations, including the Ministry of Science and Higher Education. Numerous procedural violations and systemic shortcomings were also identified.

item.title: Global Oil Prices Rise Amidst Middle East Tensions and Easing US-Iran Concerns
item.description: Global oil prices increased on November 11, recovering from previous declines. Brent crude futures rose by 0.44% to $92.44 per barrel, while WTI crude saw a 0.78% increase to $86.68 per barrel. Conversely, Russian Urals crude prices fell by 0.51% to $74.60 per barrel. The price surge is attributed to concerns over attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and easing tensions between the US and Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan Film 'Kulpaş' About Holodomor Postponed Indefinitely
item.description: The premiere of the film 'Kulpaş', scheduled for November 10, and its cinema release from November 11 have been postponed indefinitely. Directed by Akan Satayev, the film addresses the collective historical memory of the Kazakh people, focusing on the theme of famine in Kazakhstan. It is based on a story by repressed writer Beimbet Mailin.

item.title: Accountant Sentenced for Embezzling 8.3 Million Tenge in Abai Region
item.description: An accountant in the Zharma district of the Abai region has been sentenced for illegally calculating salaries for employees of a children's and youth sports school. The accountant embezzled 8.3 million tenge over two years by overpaying herself and an administrator. She was found guilty of large-scale fraud and sentenced to three years of restricted freedom.

item.title: Russian Interior Ministry Reports Sharp Decline in Migrant Crime in 2026
item.description: Crimes committed by foreign citizens in Russia decreased by 40% in the first nine months of this year compared to the same period last year, according to Russia's Interior Ministry. This decline occurs amid a notable outflow and stricter controls on migrants. Approximately 6 million foreign citizens were in Russia as of October 1, about 10% fewer than the previous year.

item.title: Kazakhstan Fails to Realize 149 Science Projects Worth 67 Billion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan has failed to implement 149 scientific and technical tasks valued at 67 billion tenge over three years. The Higher Audit Chamber reported that these tasks were often formulated vaguely, lacking specific results or implementation mechanisms. While science funding has more than doubled, the share of science in the national economy remains low at 0.16% of GDP.

item.title: Audit Reveals 51 Billion Tenge in Financial Violations in Kazakhstan's Science Funding
item.description: An audit of state budget science funding in Kazakhstan uncovered financial violations totaling 51 billion tenge and ineffective planning and use of funds amounting to 47 billion tenge. The head of the Supreme Audit Chamber noted weak demand for scientific developments from businesses, with state funding increasingly dominating. Science's share in the economy remains low at 0.16% of GDP.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airways Launches Direct Flights to Warsaw, Poland
item.description: Uzbekistan Airways has announced the sale of tickets for new direct regular flights from Tashkent to Warsaw, Poland. The inaugural flights are scheduled to commence on April 5, 2027, operating twice weekly on Mondays and Thursdays.

item.title: Rusty Hot Water in Tashkent Explained by Veolia Energy
item.description: Veolia Energy Tashkent explains that rusty hot water in Tashkent homes during the heating season is due to pressure changes and mineral deposits in pipes. While main networks are flushed, internal pipes are the responsibility of management companies.

item.title: Bank RBK Leads Major Banks in Kazakhstan for Loan Portfolio Growth
item.description: Bank RBK has emerged as the leader among major Kazakh banks in loan portfolio growth for September. The bank's portfolio increased by 5.4% to 1.8 trillion tenge, significantly exceeding the average monthly growth rate for the banking sector. Bank RBK also led in absolute growth, adding 90.3 billion tenge to its portfolio.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber Uncovers 51 Billion Tenge in Science Funding Violations
item.description: An audit by Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber revealed financial violations totaling 51 billion tenge in the science sector. Of 393 scientific tasks, 149 were not implemented. The audit also identified inefficient planning and use of funds amounting to 47 billion tenge.

item.title: Afghan Women's Rights Activists Awarded 2026 Chatham House Prize
item.description: A group of women's rights activists from Afghanistan has received the 2026 Chatham House Prize in London. The award recognizes their courage and resilience against systematic gender-based oppression and their efforts to defend the rights of women and girls.

item.title: Nearly 100 Billion Tenge in Violations and Inefficient Spending Found in Kazakh Science
item.description: Audits in Kazakhstan's science sector have uncovered nearly 100 billion tenge in violations and inefficient expenditures. These findings highlight significant issues with financial management and resource allocation within the country's scientific institutions.

item.title: Film on Chingiz Aitmatov's Premiere Postponed in Kazakhstan Amidst Censorship Fears
item.description: The premiere of a film about Kyrgyz writer Chingiz Aitmatov has been postponed in Kazakhstan from November 12 to December 3. While the reasons are not fully explained, film critics speculate potential Russian censorship, possibly related to depictions of the 1930s famine and repressions.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Urges Global Unity Against New Security Threats
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin called for coordinated international action against new security challenges at a forum in Moscow. He stressed the importance of strengthening regional cooperation and dialogue to counter threats, also noting Tajikistan's interest in Afghanistan's stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Discusses Oil, Gas, and Mining Cooperation with Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with a Saudi Arabian delegation to discuss expanding joint projects in the oil, gas, petrochemical, and mining sectors. The leaders aim to develop concrete proposals for enhanced cooperation, building on existing energy projects and growing trade relations.
